name: SC-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strongly Republican district (R+11 PVI) with an incumbent running
Huge fundraising and outside-spending advantage for Timmons
Democratic challenger is minimally funded with no outside support
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: The baseline of R+15 already reflects a favorable environment and incumbency in an R+11 district, and the money gap plus market pricing argue for moving further toward Safe R. With no polls or expert ratings, I set the margin at R+18 with modest uncertainty.
model.watch: Any late independent spending against Timmons or a surprise poll showing a single-digit race would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 4th District leans heavily Republican, with a partisan advantage of about eleven points, and incumbent William Timmons is seeking another term. The fundamentals point firmly in his direction: a favorable national environment for his party, the usual incumbency edge, and a large financial advantage. He has raised roughly $1.6 million and benefits from nearly half a million dollars in outside support, while Democrat Courtney McClain has raised about $33,000 with almost no cash on hand and no outside help.

There are no public polls or expert ratings for this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, which give Timmons about a 94 percent chance of winning. A Libertarian candidate is on the ballot but is not a factor. The expected outcome is a comfortable Republican win of roughly eighteen points.
